brief: Risk-off has retaken the rates market, reversing the prior US-led hawkish repricing of global front-ends. GS's baseline of steady growth and disinflation does not call for sharply lower yields but points to gradual relief as inflation progress shifts the policy-risk distribution and restores bonds' hedge value; a deeper setback to the AI trade would change that calculus, since AI buildout underpins broader optimism and, in turn, pricing of durably higher policy rates. In the US, firmer data, recent Fedspeak, and yields' typical lag after tighter financial conditions argue for belly (5y) outperformance, expressed via buying 3m5y vs 3m2y USD receivers (entry 0bp, target 15bp, stop -8bp). BoC hawkish rhetoric is diverging from softening Canadian data; GS expects any hawkish impulse to front-load tightening rather than extend the cycle, favoring front-end flatteners and forward longs. In Europe, November's front-end selloff reflected spillover more than domestic drivers, favoring Bund longs and further sovereign-spread tightening from lower energy prices and reduced French political risk. UK pricing through February looks too hawkish given energy-driven disinflation, favoring steepeners. In Japan, the curve should still flatten as the BoJ hikes faster than priced, favoring 2s10s flatteners (entry 94bp, target 75bp, stop 105bp).
